title: Rotate 3D points with normalized quaternions
prompt: Implement solve(payload). Input quaternion is [w,x,y,z] in scalar-first order, points is a list of 3D positions in metres, and translation is a 3D displacement in metres. Normalize the quaternion, perform its right-handed active rotation of every point, then add translation. Return {"points": [...]} in input order. Quaternion q and -q represent the same rotation. If its Euclidean norm is <=1e-12 return {"error":"zero_quaternion"}, including for empty points. Quaternion components have magnitude at most 1e6. Do not round output. Any numeric inputs are finite; inputs have the documented shapes; unspecified validation is out of scope. Do not mutate payload or any nested value. Numeric absolute tolerance 1e-9, relative tolerance 1e-9; strings, booleans, errors and collection shapes must match exactly.
bad_solution:
def solve(payload):
    return {"points": [[p[i]+payload["translation"][i] for i in range(3)] for p in payload["points"]]}
